comments.author: @Infinity269
comments.text: Business implications for OpenAI and Microsoft are massive. They made this model free to access without an account. That means that every person who interacts with it that doesn't specifically opt out will be providing multimodal training data for iterative improvement. And the ability to watch someone's screen and see what they do after the model tells them how to perform an operation or do some function means thousands of hours of training data on direct digital action over multistep workflows per day. And the same comes from their business partnerships (though not enterprise unless the company opts in). No wonder they aren't worried about not having access to any private training sets. They are never going to run out of training data again.

comments.author: @neiljamessloan
comments.text:
Love your channel. May I suggest? When you're using another video from another source within your own video could you consider...?

" Pushing back" the video presented into a container? 
So not to present the video into full screen?

I know this may seem like a mute or insignificant point. However, if you present another video in your own presentations (in full-screen) it appears like you are "advocating" for that video.

It's basically not a necessity to 'fullscreen' another video into one's own video presentation.

 In simpler words... try putting the video into your presentation in its own container/frame. Maintaining a sense of objectivity.
That way we don't get confused about intention and can distinguish that you are not simply mirroring a video for your own purposes or just reproducing a video in your own context.

Best always :)

Keep up your work in educating us people about the AI landscape.

Peace
